headline: Automated traffic camera ordinance failed 3-3, while a Police Chief salary budget correction passed and the PY52 action plan was referred back to committee.
summary: Residents spoke at public input sessions held by several committees. Most consent calendar items passed, including agreements for Hamden Middle School and a Youth Diversion Team extension. The Hamden Ice Rink management agreement stayed in committee, and the Laurel View Golf Course lease change was not voted on.
decisions: Approved eight remaining consent calendar items unanimously, including Hamden Middle School agreements, Fire Station #2 funding, and the Axon body camera purchase.
Approved reclassifying uncollectable taxes to the suspense tax book, unanimously.
Approved the mayor signing a U.S. Department of Energy assistance agreement for energy efficiency improvements at the Administrative Building, unanimously.
Approved Community Investment Fund Round 7 funds for Newhall Foundations construction, 13 in favor, with 1 abstention.
Approved the mayor entering into an agreement with Hamden Newhall Neighborhood Association, Inc., 13 in favor, with 1 abstention.
Approved a bid waiver for Hamden Newhall Neighborhood Association, Inc., 14-0.
Approved extending the agreement with CT VIP Youth Services Bureau's Youth Diversion Team, 13 in favor, with 1 abstention.
Approved creating a youth engagement gift account and accepting a donation from the Jeet Patel Foundation for the police department, unanimously.
Referred the PY52 Annual Action Plan back to committee to add more community outreach, 10 in favor and 4 opposed.
Kept the Hamden Ice Rink management agreement amendment in committee for the next meeting, with no vote taken.
Approved amending the 2026-2027 budget to correct the Police Chief's salary, 5 in favor, 3 opposed, with 1 abstention.
Approved an interdepartmental transfer of 2025-2026 budget funds for the Town Attorney, 8 in favor with 1 abstention.
Approved an interdepartmental transfer to pay May/June streetlighting utility costs, unanimously.
Voted 5 in favor and 1 opposed to untable the amendment to the automated traffic enforcement ordinance.
Failed 3-3 on the motion for the automated traffic enforcement ordinance amendment, so the motion fails.

1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
Public Works & Sustainability Committee Special Meeting, August 3, 2026.  The meeting 
was called to order at 6:05pm with the members noted above in attendance. Council 
members Teodosio, Crouch, Alston were absent. 
  
2. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION 
Public Comment was opened at 6:55pm.  One person gave public comment.  
  
3. HAMDEN ICE RINK 
Chair Stevens explained that, because some committee members were unable to attend 
the meeting, no vote would be taken this evening. He stated that the Committee would 
proceed with the presentation so the information could be placed on the record, and the 
absent members would have the opportunity to review it before the item was considered 
at a future meeting. He then invited the management company to begin its presentation.  
  1. Q&A Rink Management Company Hamden Ice Rink 
Representatives of the rink management company provided an overview of the 
history of the management agreement, including the division of maintenance 
responsibilities and revenue sharing under the various agreements. They also 
described the rink's operations, scheduling, marketing efforts, financial reporting 
process, and maintenance responsibilities, including routine upkeep and the current 
condition of major equipment. Committee Members also asked questions on future 
capital needs. 
  
  2. UNTABLE FOR ACTION: ORDER APPROVING AN AMENDMENT AND 
EXTENSION OF MANAGEMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE TOWN 
OF HAMDEN AND 595 MIX AVENUE LLC - ICE RINK 
Since the item was not going to be voted on during this evening’s meeting, it was not 
untabled.  Chair Stevens noted that he would like the item to remain in Committee to 
be heard at the next Committee meeting.
4. UNFINISHED BUSINESS  
  1. ORDER AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE A LEASE 
MODIFICATION FOR LAUREL VIEW GOLF COURSE 
Chair Stevens explained that the Committee was still awaiting additional information 
on the proposed Laurel View Golf Course lease modification and was not prepared to 
vote on the item that evening. He then invited the Chief of Staff to provide an update. 
 
Chief of Staff Peterson reported that the Administration continued to negotiate the 
proposed lease modification with the lessee and counsel for both parties and 
anticipated bringing a final agreement to the Council as soon as practicable. She 
explained that the proposed lease extension would transfer responsibility for 
maintaining the entry roads and parking areas to the lessee, reducing the Town's 
financial and operational obligations while providing the lessee with the opportunity to 
recover its investment through the extended lease term. She also noted that 
supporting photographs had been provided to illustrate improvements previously 
made to the property. 
 
ADJOURN 
Reiterating that they were not ready to vote on either of the agenda items, Chair 
Stevens adjourned the meeting at 7:10pm.

3. ACTION ITEM  
  1. 
UNTABLE AMENDMENT AND RESTATEMENT OF CHAPTER 73 OF THE CODE OF 
ORDINANCES ESTABLISHING THE USE OF AUTOMATED TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT 
SAFETY DEVICES IN THE TOWN OF HAMDEN PURSUANT TO THE AUTHORITY 
GRANTED IN PUBLIC ACT 23-116, AN ACT IMPLEMENTING THE 
RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE VISION ZERO COUNCIL 
Chair Foley called for a motion to untable item 3.1: 
Motion: Figlar 
Second: Parks 
 
Roll Call Vote:  
Doug Foley – Yes 
Grace Teodosio – Yes 
Tom Figlar – Yes 
Tameeka Park – Yes 
Sarah Gallagher – Yes 
Bob Anthony – No 
Vote: 5 in favor of untabiling and 1 opposed (Anthony).
Chair Foley then asked for a motion to open the item so that the Committee could 
begin debate and discussion: 
Motion: Gallagher 
Second: Figlar  
 
Council Members engaged in a lengthy discussion regarding the automated traffic 
enforcement program, raising questions about the scope (beyond safety), the 
collection, protection, and retention of personal information, the payment processing 
vendor, and the distribution of camera locations.  During the discussion, Chief of Staff 
Peterson reminded the Committee that the proposed ordinance amendment was 
limited to revisions to the hearing process for automated traffic enforcement 
violations.  President Kiely asked for clarification on whether the amendment is 
actually amending the traffic camera ordinance or is it amending an ordinance on 
hearings in general.  Attorney Gruen was unavailable to provide the answer, but 
President Keily said it could be address if the item passed to the full Council. 
With no additional discussion, Chair Foley took a roll call vote: 
 
Roll Call Vote:  
Doug Foley – Yes 
Grace Teodosio – No 
Tom Figlar – No 
Tameeka Park – Yes 
Sarah Gallagher – Yes 
Bob Anthony – No 
 
Vote: 3 in favor, 3 opposed (Anthony, Teodosio, Figlar).  The vote is a tie; the motion 
fails. 
       
      
ADJOURN 
Chair Foley made a motion to adjourn. 
Second: Figlar 
Vote: All were in favor, and the IT & Civic Engagement Committee meeting was adjourned at 
8:40pm.
